Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and location. We adapt the length, level and language, and prepare a quotation. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

Rather than a rapid tour of a whole museum, this visit concentrates on a single gallery chosen with you. An archaeologist takes the group through about a dozen objects: what each is, how it was made and found, and what it tells us.

The gallery, date, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • One gallery, chosen with you beforehand
  • About a dozen objects, each looked at slowly
  • How to read a museum label, and what it leaves out
  • Questions you can carry into any other gallery

How the time is spent

  1. Gallery orientation 20 min

    Agree chosen museum/theme and collections.

    You: questions list

  2. Object reading 55 min

    Read labels, provenance and chronology.

    You: object sheet

  3. Comparison 45 min

    Select 2–3 related objects.

    You: comparison grid

  4. Reflection 30 min

    Write museum interpretation label.

    You: label draft

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Read a museum label for provenance and chronology, and notice what it leaves out.
  • Describe what an object is, how it was made and how it was found.
  • Compare two or three related objects and draft an interpretation label of your own.

You take away

A portfolio of your work from each session.
